manual:
**Game plan:** faster "fair" deck — tutor the right Warrior, apply board+hand pressure, still keep the Chaos/Metamorphosis reach.

**Key cards / engine:** Reinforcement of the Army toolbox; Marauding Captain; D.D. Warrior Lady; BLS.

**How to pilot / combo lines:**
- **`Reinforcement of the Army` is your answer tutor** — fetch `D.D. Warrior Lady` into a big beater (banishes both in battle — denies the opponent's Chaos fuel), `Exiled Force` to pop a problem, or `Marauding Captain` to develop.
- **`Marauding Captain` doubles up:** on Normal Summon it Special Summons a Level-4-or-lower monster from hand [CDB], so one card becomes two bodies, and while it's up the opponent "cannot target Warrior monsters for attacks, except this one" [CDB] — your backrow-light board survives a turn.
- **`Blade Knight` is 2000 ATK when you hold ≤1 card**, so empty your hand into the board and let it close; `Don Zaloog` chips the hand/deck on damage; `Exarion Universe` pierces defense.
- Lead with `Trap Dustshoot` where possible to strip their key card and read the game plan; use `Book of Moon`/`Sakuretsu` to punch a lane open, then race.
- The `Scapegoat`→`Metamorphosis`→TER package is still here as a defensive reset when the race stalls — same two-turn timing as Goat Control.

**Weaknesses:** thinner trap suite than Control means it folds to a bigger control deck's grind if the aggression stalls; mass removal (`Torrential`, `Mirror Force`) punishes over-committing your Warriors.

=== EXTRA DECK ===

**Your only door is `Metamorphosis` — "Tribute 1 monster. Special Summon 1 Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck with the same Level as the Tributed monster" [CDB].** No `Polymerization`, no `Cyber-Stein`, and `Magical Scientist` is **Forbidden** in GOAT [GF-BAN]. Tokens are legal material ("including a Sheep Token from `Scapegoat`"), Metamorphosis "cannot be activated" if no Fusion in the list matches the tributed monster's Level, and it "does not properly Summon a Fusion Monster, so you cannot use `Monster Reborn` on it afterwards" [GR].

**⚠ Level audit — apart from two monsters this deck tops out at Level 4. Lv1:** Sheep Token, `Sinister Serpent`, `Magician of Faith`. **Lv6:** `Chaos Sorcerer`. **Lv5 and Lv9: nothing.** `Premature Burial` and `Call of the Haunted` only target *your* Graveyard [CDB], so `Snatch Steal` on an opposing Level 5 is the only way to hold one.

- **`Thousand-Eyes Restrict` (Lv1)** — the reason the Scapegoat package sits in a Warrior deck at all: "the most frequent and most powerful fusion monster special summoned with Metamorphosis … it can take the opponent's best monster while locking down the field at the same time" [GF-FUS]. Goats in the opponent's End Phase [GW], token → Metamorphosis on your turn, then **absorb with priority** — in GOAT rules "when a Chain or Summon has finished resolving, the turn player can activate a fast effect *or a monster's Ignition Effect* before the opponent is allowed to respond" [GF-BASICS], so equip the instant Metamorphosis resolves, before `Book of Moon` can land; if they flip it down first, TER "needs to be face up on the field to attach a monster to itself, so its effect will fizzle" [GR]. ⚠ TER freezes *your* Warriors too — it is the reset button when the race stalls, not a way to keep beating down. `Tsukuyomi` is not in this list, so you get one absorb, not a loop.
- **`Ryu Senshi` (Lv6) off `Chaos Sorcerer` — your kill-turn enabler**, "the most commonly used level 6 fusion monster, and it [is] mostly used for setting up kill turns via Chaos Sorcerer+Metamorphosis" [GF-FUS]. It pays 1000 LP to negate a **Normal Trap** (`Mirror Force`, `Torrential Tribute`, `Sakuretsu Armor`, `Ring of Destruction` — *not* the Counter Trap `Solemn Judgment`) and "negate[s] the effects of any Spell Card that targets this card and destroy[s] it" [CDB], walking through `Book of Moon` and `Snatch Steal` — exactly the removal a wide Warrior board dies to. Sorcerer "cannot attack the turn you activate this effect" [CDB], so the swap costs you nothing on a turn you banish.
- **`Dark Balter the Terrible` (Lv5) — only off a *stolen* Level 5:** "after Thousand-Eyes Restrict, this is the most commonly used fusion monster brought forth with Metamorphosis … the potential to negate both spells and monster effects is quite powerful" [GF-FUS], and it is normally made off `Airknight Parshath` [GW], which this deck does not run. The live line is the one the format guide describes literally: `Snatch Steal` their `Airknight Parshath` (or any Level 5), then Metamorphosis it [GF-FUS]. Payoff: it pays 1000 LP to negate a Normal Spell (`Pot of Greed`, `Graceful Charity`, `Heavy Storm`, `Nobleman of Crossout`) and negates the effect of any Effect Monster it kills in battle [CDB].
- **`Musician King` (Lv5) — the LIGHT slot, same `Snatch Steal` line.** A 1750 vanilla you make purely for the Graveyard: "in the rare situations where you have `Snatch Steal` for your opponent's `Airknight Parshath` and need to Metamorphosis for a light monster in your graveyard for a chaos monster [it] could be the difference between winning and losing the game" [GF-FUS]. Their monster returns to *their* Graveyard when you tribute it, so the LIGHT you bank is the Fusion itself when it dies — which is what re-arms `Chaos Sorcerer`/`BLS` ("1 LIGHT and 1 DARK" banished [CDB]) after `D.D. Warrior Lady` and `Blade Knight` have already been spent. That guide picks `Giltia the D. Knight` (also LIGHT, Level 5, 1850 ATK) for this slot and never names Musician King — same job, 100 more ATK.
- **`Master of Oz` (Lv9) — ⚠ dead card in this build.** It is "a common Cyber-Stein target" [GF-FUS], but this deck runs **no `Cyber-Stein`** and has no Level 9 monster, so there is no legal way to put it on the field. Cut it, or add `Cyber-Stein`.
